sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Like many teens in the 80s, my first job was at the mall.
sentences.zh: 和许多80年代的青少年一样，我的第一份工作是在商场里。

sentences.en: I was 14.
sentences.zh: 那时我14岁。

sentences.en: I lied about my age.
sentences.zh: 我谎报了年龄。

sentences.en: I was a busboy in an Applebee's-style restaurant that no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 我在一家早已不复存在的苹果蜂式餐厅当服务生。

sentences.en: On Saturdays, I often worked three shifts in a row,
sentences.zh: 周六时，我经常连续上三个班，

sentences.en: so I witnessed the entire circadian rhythm of the mall.
sentences.zh: 所以我见证了商场完整的昼夜节律。

sentences.en: At 8 o'clock, I'd clean windows as the senior citizens in tracksuits
sentences.zh: 早上8点，我会擦窗户，看着那些穿着运动服的老年人

sentences.en: powered through the empty halls, passing by shops with their cage doors still rolled down.
sentences.zh: 在空荡荡的大厅里大步流星，经过一家家还没卷起铁闸门的店铺。

sentences.en: By midday, the families took over,
sentences.zh: 到了中午，家庭客群接管了这里，

sentences.en: and my usual job of clearing glasses and plates
sentences.zh: 我日常清理杯盘的工作，

sentences.en: involved cleaning up piles of food spilled on the floor.
sentences.zh: 还包括清理地上洒得到处都是的食物残渣。

sentences.en: By evening, the teens arrived.
sentences.zh: 到了傍晚，青少年们来了。

sentences.en: They couldn't afford the restaurant,
sentences.zh: 他们消费不起餐厅，

sentences.en: but I could see them in packs, congregating by the fountain,
sentences.zh: 但我能看到他们成群结队地聚集在喷泉旁，

sentences.en: always ready with an unkind word for some act of cruelty.
sentences.zh: 随时准备对某种残忍的行为吐出刻薄的言语。

sentences.en: The mall felt terrible.
sentences.zh: 那时的商场感觉糟透了。

sentences.en: I hated it.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌它。

sentences.en: But despite this, on days when I wasn't working,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，在我不上班的日子里，

sentences.en: I had my mom drop me off at the mall.
sentences.zh: 我还是会让妈妈把我送到商场。

sentences.en: Kids in small towns and suburbs play the hand they're dealt,
sentences.zh: 小城镇和郊区的孩子们只能接受命运的安排，

sentences.en: and being able to walk around on your own,
sentences.zh: 而能够独自四处走走，

sentences.en: maybe buying a cassette tape of the Smith's Live album at Sam Goody,
sentences.zh: 或许在Sam Goody买一张史密斯乐队的现场专辑磁带，

sentences.en: is the best that life has to offer.
sentences.zh: 就是生活所能提供的最美好的事了。

sentences.en: I was not a very cool teen.
sentences.zh: 我不是一个很酷的少年。

sentences.en: Let me just say, I was a very nerdy teen.
sentences.zh: 我得说，我是一个非常书呆子气的少年。

sentences.en: This is cool adult and friend of the show,
sentences.zh: 这位是酷酷的成年人，也是本节目的朋友，

sentences.en: Alexander Lang.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉·朗。

sentences.en: I feel like there are a lot of teenage mall scenarios
sentences.zh: 我觉得有很多关于青少年逛商场的场景，

sentences.en: that I did not participate in.
sentences.zh: 我都没有参与过。

sentences.en: Like, I did not, like, meet my first beau at the mall.
sentences.zh: 比如，我没有在商场里遇到我的初恋。

sentences.en: I did not, like, stroll around with shopping bags,
sentences.zh: 我也没有拎着购物袋四处闲逛，

sentences.en: showing off at the mall.
sentences.zh: 在商场里炫耀。

sentences.en: None of that.
sentences.zh: 这些都没有。

sentences.en: But no teen in the 80s could completely avoid the gravitational pull of the mall.
sentences.zh: 但80年代没有哪个青少年能完全逃脱商场的引力。

sentences.en: Alexandra is the author of a new book called Meet Me by the Fountain.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉是一本名为《在喷泉旁见》的新书的作者。

sentences.en: I think part of the whole argument of this book is really that people are social creatures,
sentences.zh: 我想这本书的核心论点之一，其实就是人类是社交动物，

sentences.en: and that the mall had to be created because the suburbs didn't really initially, like,
sentences.zh: 而商场的诞生是因为郊区最初并没有真正考虑到，

sentences.en: think about a space for people to come together.
sentences.zh: 要为人们提供一个聚会的空间。

sentences.en: Even though we're past the heyday of the mall,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们已经过了商场的全盛时期，

sentences.en: Alexandra says we haven't seen the death of the mall,
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉说我们并没有看到商场的消亡，

sentences.en: even after two and a half years of a global pandemic.
sentences.zh: 即使是在经历了两年半的全球大流行之后。

sentences.en: I think that people are people,
sentences.zh: 我认为人终究是人，

sentences.en: and they're going to want to, like, go back out and get together again.
sentences.zh: 他们还是会想要走出去，再次聚在一起。

sentences.en: I think we've seen that in, like, the tremendous use of parks during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在大流行期间公园的使用率激增中已经看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And when we can safely gather indoors, like, people are going to be excited to do that
sentences.zh: 当我们可以安全地在室内聚集时，人们会很兴奋地去做这件事，

sentences.en: because who wants to go to a park in December?
sentences.zh: 因为谁想在十二月去公园呢？

sentences.en: We're going to talk about how the mall became a ubiquitous part of American culture
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论商场是如何成为美国文化中无处不在的一部分，

sentences.en: and what's happening today as malls across the country start to disappear.
sentences.zh: 以及当全国各地的商场开始消失时，今天正在发生什么。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's get down to some basics.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们从一些基本概念开始。

sentences.en: What is a mall?
sentences.zh: 什么是商场？

sentences.en: What makes something a mall versus other shopping centers that existed before or after?
sentences.zh: 是什么让一个地方成为商场，而不是之前或之后存在的其他购物中心？

sentences.en: Well, a shopping center is outdoors and a mall is indoors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，购物中心是露天的，而商场是室内的。

sentences.en: That's the most basic thing.
sentences.zh: 这是最基本的区别。

sentences.en: A shopping center is a strip mall or a line of stores facing the parking lot
sentences.zh: 购物中心通常是带状商场，或者是一排排面向停车场的商店，

sentences.en: with some sort of, like, covering over the space in front of them,
sentences.zh: 前面可能有一些遮盖物，

sentences.en: whereas a mall is indoors.
sentences.zh: 而商场是在室内的。

sentences.en: And the earliest malls were basically just, like, two shopping strips put together.
sentences.zh: 最早的商场基本上就是把两条购物街拼在一起。

sentences.en: So you had a department store at each end and then two lines of shops facing each other
sentences.zh: 两端各有一家百货公司，中间是两排相对的商店，

sentences.en: and a covered, you know, central aisle that usually had fountains and plants and benches
sentences.zh: 以及一条有顶棚的中央通道，通常配有喷泉、植物、长椅

sentences.en: and other amenities.
sentences.zh: 和其他便利设施。

sentences.en: So they were really just that super simple kind of eye-shaped plan.
sentences.zh: 所以它们本质上就是那种超级简单的眼形平面布局。

sentences.en: And this shape, the long hallway, is where the word mall comes from.
sentences.zh: 而这种长廊的形状，正是“mall”这个词的由来。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Basically, the name mall comes from Paul Mall in London, which is a narrow street where they used
sentences.zh: 基本上，“mall”这个名字来源于伦敦的“Pall Mall”，那是一条狭窄的街道，人们过去常在那里

sentences.en: to play a kind of bowling game.
sentences.zh: 玩一种类似保龄球的游戏。

sentences.en: So it was this long, narrow outdoor space where people would come together to play.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一个人们聚集玩耍的狭长户外空间。

sentences.en: And so the mall from Paul Mall turned into a landscape term for that kind of long, narrow green space.
sentences.zh: 因此，“mall”从“Pall Mall”演变成了一个景观术语，指代那种狭长的绿地。

sentences.en: So then when you enclose that long, narrow space under a roof, it is another kind of mall.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你把那个狭长的空间用屋顶围起来时，它就成了另一种形式的“mall”。

sentences.en: So the mall in Washington is also a mall from the same origin, even though we don't really think
sentences.zh: 所以华盛顿的国家广场（The Mall）也是同一个词源，尽管我们并不会真的

sentences.en: about a shopping mall and the mall in Washington in the same mental place.
sentences.zh: 把购物商场和华盛顿的国家广场放在同一个心理范畴里。

sentences.en: Right, that place with the reflecting pool and the Lincoln on one side.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是那个有倒影池和林肯像的那一边。

sentences.en: That's the Capitol Mall.
sentences.zh: 那是国会大厦广场。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Lincoln is the anchor store of the National Mall.
sentences.zh: 林肯是国家广场的“主力店”。

sentences.en: He's the Macy's of the Capitol Mall.
sentences.zh: 他是国会大厦广场的梅西百货。

sentences.en: So Victor Gruen is credited as the father of the mall.
sentences.zh: 所以维克多·格鲁恩被誉为“商场之父”。

sentences.en: What was he trying to do?
sentences.zh: 他当时想做什么？

sentences.en: What was he trying to make?
sentences.zh: 他想创造什么？

sentences.en: So Gruen was an emigre from Austria, fled the Nazis to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩是一位来自奥地利的移民，为了逃避纳粹来到美国，

sentences.en: in the late 1930s.
sentences.zh: 时间是在20世纪30年代末。

sentences.en: And he had really strong memories of the kind of charming streets of Vienna, where there are cafes and, you know,
sentences.zh: 他对维也纳那种迷人的街道有着深刻的记忆，那里有咖啡馆，人们

sentences.en: people gather at fountains and there's this whole rich outdoor life.
sentences.zh: 在喷泉旁聚会，有着丰富多彩的户外生活。

sentences.en: So he came to America.
sentences.zh: 所以他来到了美国。

sentences.en: He initially designed these very glamorous stores in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 他最初在曼哈顿设计了一些非常迷人的商店。

sentences.en: And then he was taken up by some department store executives who were like, move to California, design our department stores.
sentences.zh: 后来他被一些百货公司高管看中，他们说：“搬到加州来，设计我们的百货公司吧。”

sentences.en: So he started designing these freestanding department stores.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始设计这些独立的百货公司。

sentences.en: And he just felt kind of crushed by the landscape around those department stores.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得被那些百货公司周围的景观压得喘不过气来。

sentences.en: Because you could go to the store and you could park and you could go in.
sentences.zh: 因为你可以开车去商店，停车，然后进去。

sentences.en: But then you couldn't do anything else.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，你什么也做不了。

sentences.en: Like you couldn't leave and sit at a cafe.
sentences.zh: 你没法离开商店去咖啡馆坐坐。

sentences.en: There was nowhere to meet your friends.
sentences.zh: 没有地方可以见朋友。

sentences.en: There was none of the kind of fabric of the city that he found in European cities.
sentences.zh: 没有他在欧洲城市里感受到的那种城市肌理。

sentences.en: So in the early 1940s, Gruen was living in New York and flying back and forth across the country a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪40年代初，格鲁恩住在纽约，经常在全国各地飞来飞去。

sentences.en: Like major, major airplane miles.
sentences.zh: 飞行里程非常惊人。

sentences.en: And he gets stuck in Detroit on a cross-country flight because of fog.
sentences.zh: 有一次因为大雾，他在底特律的转机途中被困住了。

sentences.en: And he thinks, oh, okay, like I'm not going to waste this time I have on the ground in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 他想，好吧，我不能浪费在底特律停留的这段时间。

sentences.en: You know, it's like he asked his friends, where is life happening?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他问朋友们，生活都在哪里发生？

sentences.en: In Detroit.
sentences.zh: 在底特律。

sentences.en: And they said, oh, it's all out in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，都在郊区。

sentences.en: So he gets driven around the suburbs and he finds what he's been finding elsewhere in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 于是他被带着在郊区转了一圈，他发现了他在美国其他地方看到的情况：

sentences.en: That, yes, there are all these new houses and, yes, there are all these strip malls, but there's nowhere to go.
sentences.zh: 是的，这里有许多新房子，也有许多带状商场，但根本没地方可去。

sentences.en: And he thinks that he, you know, master salesman, he should be able to sell J.L.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己，你知道，作为顶级推销员，他应该能说服J.L.

sentences.en: Hudson on the idea of building a branched apartment store and a shopping center in the suburbs.
sentences.zh: Hudson百货公司接受在郊区建立分支百货和购物中心的想法。

sentences.en: And over the next several years, he does this.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，他做到了。

sentences.en: He actually sells them on the idea of building four of them.
sentences.zh: 他实际上说服了他们建造四个这样的中心。

sentences.en: Northland, Southland, Eastland, and Westland.
sentences.zh: Northland、Southland、Eastland和Westland。

sentences.en: Yeah, I've always wondered about that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我一直对这个很好奇。

sentences.en: Like, why do so many malls have cardinal directions in the name?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么多商场名字里都有方位词？

sentences.en: Like, no matter what city you're in, they're all like Westfield or Southport.
sentences.zh: 不管你在哪个城市，它们都叫Westfield或者Southport之类的。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么？

sentences.en: This is the origin story.
sentences.zh: 这就是起源故事。

sentences.en: And this is one way in which I know, like, the book can be slightly confusing because all the malls sound the same.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我知道这本书可能会让人有点困惑，因为所有的商场听起来都一样。

sentences.en: And it's like, yeah, that was on purpose.
sentences.zh: 就像是，没错，那是故意的。

sentences.en: Yes, because the, you know, if you're thinking about your city with the center point downtown,
sentences.zh: 是的，因为如果你以市中心为中心点来思考你的城市，

sentences.en: all of these malls wanted to establish where they were in relation to that center point.
sentences.zh: 所有这些商场都想确立它们相对于那个中心点的位置。

sentences.en: So if you were driving north on the kind of main highway out of town, you would encounter Northland or North Park or Northfield or Northdale or one of these other things.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你沿着出城的主干道向北行驶，你就会遇到Northland、North Park、Northfield、Northdale或其他类似的名字。

sentences.en: You know, same with South, East, or WeSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，南、东、西也是一样。

sentences.en: So all of them are, like, named after the cardinal points so that people know kind of where to find them in relation to downtown.
sentences.zh: 所以它们都以方位命名，这样人们就知道相对于市中心该去哪里找它们。

sentences.en: And then the second part of the word is gate because it's an entry to the city.
sentences.zh: 名字的后半部分，“gate”是因为它是通往城市的入口。

sentences.en: It's land because that was open land before.
sentences.zh: “land”是因为以前那是空地。

sentences.en: It's park because they're attaching it to a parkway.
sentences.zh: “park”是因为它们连接着公园大道。

sentences.en: Like, they have kind of, you know, vague geographical associations.
sentences.zh: 它们都有一些模糊的地理联想。

sentences.en: The problem really comes that, like, I grew up going to Northgate Mall in Durham, North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题在于，我是在北卡罗来纳州达勒姆的Northgate商场长大的。

sentences.en: But there's a much more famous Northgate Mall in Seattle that was one of the first malls.
sentences.zh: 但西雅图有一个更著名的Northgate商场，它是最早的商场之一。

sentences.en: And it's like, so you always have to specify, you know, which city you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以你总是得说明你在说哪个城市。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it feels like there's a certain point where the naming convention becomes just a meaningless convention.
sentences.zh: 而且感觉在某个时刻，这种命名惯例就变成了一种毫无意义的习俗。

sentences.en: Like, one of the fancier malls in downtown San Francisco is called Westfield.
sentences.zh: 比如，旧金山市中心最高档的商场之一叫Westfield。

sentences.en: I don't think it's west of anything or a field at all.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得它在什么东西的西边，也不觉得它有什么田野。

sentences.en: But, you know, maybe that's just, I don't know, maybe you know.
sentences.zh: 但也许，我不知道，也许你知道。

sentences.en: No, no, Westfield is actually a huge mall conglomerate that's now owned by Australians.
sentences.zh: 不，不，Westfield实际上是一个巨大的商场集团，现在由澳大利亚人拥有。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: But Westfield may be originally named after a Westfield that was in some town.
sentences.zh: 但Westfield最初可能也是以某个城镇里的Westfield命名的。

sentences.en: So Gruen designed these malls in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 格鲁恩在密歇根州设计了这些商场。

sentences.en: And he saw the early mall as more of a mixed-use hub.
sentences.zh: 他将早期的商场视为一种混合用途的中心。

sentences.en: There were shops and apartment stores, but also post offices and doctor's offices.
sentences.zh: 那里不仅有商店和百货公司，还有邮局和医生诊所。

sentences.en: How long did that idea of a mall last?
sentences.zh: 那种商场的理念持续了多久？

sentences.en: Yeah, Gruen definitely saw the malls as having a community function.
sentences.zh: 是的，格鲁恩确实认为商场具有社区功能。

sentences.en: And that's really explicit in a lot of his writings in the 1940s and 1950s.
sentences.zh: 这在他20世纪40和50年代的许多著作中都有明确体现。

sentences.en: And he wasn't alone in that.
sentences.zh: 而且他并不孤单。

sentences.en: There are other early mall developers, including James Rouse, who comes back into the story later,
sentences.zh: 还有其他早期的商场开发商，包括詹姆斯·劳斯，他稍后会出现在我们的故事中，

sentences.en: who also built malls, you know, circa 1955, 1956, that had community spaces.
sentences.zh: 他也建造了商场，你知道，大约在1955年、1956年，这些商场都有社区空间。

sentences.en: They might have church spaces.
sentences.zh: 它们可能设有教堂空间。

sentences.en: They definitely had doctor's offices.
sentences.zh: 它们绝对有医生诊所。

sentences.en: A lot of malls also had nurseries.
sentences.zh: 许多商场还设有托儿所。

sentences.en: So these early malls had a lot more community functions built in, and they were thought of as
sentences.zh: 所以这些早期的商场内置了更多的社区功能，它们被认为是

sentences.en: replacing downtown.
sentences.zh: 市中心的替代品。

sentences.en: And so having these mixed-use functions.
sentences.zh: 所以才有了这些混合用途的功能。

sentences.en: But what happened was over time, like by the mid-1960s, there just start to be more and more
sentences.zh: 但后来发生的情况是，随着时间的推移，大约到了20世纪60年代中期，开始出现了越来越多

sentences.en: malls.
sentences.zh: 的购物中心。

sentences.en: And they're not being designed and created by these original developers.
sentences.zh: 而且它们不再是由最初的那些开发商来设计和建造的了。

sentences.en: And the developers just want to make money.
sentences.zh: 开发商们只是想赚钱。

sentences.en: And they've also found that, you know, the mall has been kind of incorporated as an American
sentences.zh: 他们还发现，你知道，购物中心已经以某种方式融入了美国人的

sentences.en: pastime.
sentences.zh: 消遣生活中。

sentences.en: And it turns out you don't need to have a community space for your mall to operate like a community
